title: Unsigned c.e. representability does not justify the claimed pruned subtree of a PA completion.
details: Cenzer–Remmel2017, Theorem3.4.8 proof p112. From a formula representing the c.e. set of nodes with finite cones, the proof defines a subtree by excluding every node whose deadness sentence belongs to the consistent arithmetic extension Gamma, then asserts that the resulting tree has no dead ends. Consistency alone does not prevent Gamma from containing false Sigma1 deadness assertions. For example, take the computable consistency tree for PA and a consistent completion of PA plus not-Con(PA); the standard dead-root sentence can be the false Sigma1 assertion that PA has a contradiction proof, which that completion contains, so the proposed pruning can discard the root of a nonempty path class. The proof needs a two-sided finite-witness comparison construction whose provable alternatives preserve at least one infinite child, or an explicit separator construction using numeralwise representation and finite cuts. The corpus PA-degree handoff uses the latter and does not assume Sigma1 soundness of an arbitrary consistent completion.
